# `pattern-removed`

Pattern removed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `pattern-removed` (both directions), `pattern-removed-in-request`, `pattern-removed-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A `pattern` was removed.

## Why this default

In requests: more values are valid. In responses: clients that parse values by the old pattern may fail.

## Example

From test case [`pattern-removed`](../../test/cases/pattern-removed/): A pattern removed from a response string.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
-           pattern: ^[a-z]+$
```

Findings:

- `pattern-removed-in-response` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  pattern-removed: warn
```

## How to fix

Keep the pattern in responses if clients rely on it.
